articles.title: Can AI data centers be mass-produced like cars? This startup aims to find out | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Runware is building a factory to turn out prefabricated AI data centers on an assembly line. The real test will be whether it can deliver at that scale.
articles.body_text: AI infrastructure company Runware is making news again, just months after unveiling the Sonic Inference Pod, a modular data center built in a factory and shipped to customers ready to install. Now the company has bigger plans. It told TechCrunch it wants to build a factory that assembles these pods on a production line, as if they were cars. The idea isn’t entirely new. Companies like Crusoe and Schneider Electric also sell prefabricated pods, but Runware says it can ship its pods faster. Flaviu Radulescu, co-founder and CEO of Runware, told TechCrunch that the company plans to scale production at its Romania-based factory to 30 megawatts of data center capacity per day by 2028, or nearly 1 gigawatt per month. That’s a whole lot of capacity: at that pace, Runware would produce roughly as much in a year as the entire U.S. was expected to add in data center power this year, about 10 gigawatts . But it also reflects an industry-wide push to deploy data centers faster more efficiently. Nvidia announced, for example, the Vera Rubin AI factories and the DSX POD earlier this year. Both are also meant to make it faster and easier for companies to build their own AI data centers. The difference with Runware, though, is that it says it has actually built a factory rather than just designed the infrastructure that would let others build one. Radulescu said Runware will gradually increase production starting next year and that it already has two factories — one it has used for a few years to build the pods, and a second it started building earlier this year. The second is expected to be finished within months and go online early next year. Runware will manufacture the modular data centers on an assembly line. Customers can provide their own site to assemble them, or Runware can find one for them. Radulescu said Runware aims to bring the pods online within 48 hours. That time covers installation and set-up time, not build time. A pod once took three weeks to build but it will soon take one day as it ramps up production, says the company. Runware will provide spare parts if components fail. Customers can also rent compute from Runware or supply their own GPUs and pay a monthly fee for the pods and operations. Power and internet are charged separately, he said. The pods can also be customized to customer preferences, he said. The pods have a standard design, but can be configured to meet customer requirements and the latest GPU chips. Chips can take a long time to arrive after they’re ordered, which works in Runware’s favor. “Our pod delivery times are also shorter than current GPU lead times, giving us time to adapt the infrastructure to the hardware being ordered,” he said. “For new GPU generations, our in-house hardware team can design, build, and test components itself, allowing us to adapt quickly.” Right now, these are all plans — execution is the test. The factory will need a lot of people, inventory, supply chain logistics, and money. There are cautionary tales about reinventing manufacturing, notably the electric vehicle startup Arrival, once valued at over $13 billion , which struggled to mass-produce electric vehicles cost-effectively compared with traditional plants. Runware, which has raised more than $60 million to date, said it plans to raise a Series B, but for now it is finishing and launching the factory with the $50 million Series A it raised last December. “Our cost structure is very different,” Radulescu said, explaining how Runware seeks to avoid Arrival’s fate. “We do have headcount and materials cost,” he continued. “But our factory staff is cost-effective relative to the value of deploying compute for AI.” He also said that designing its own systems and buying widely available, affordable parts helps keep costs low. “We’ve brought in a highly experienced plant manager from the automotive industry to work alongside our chief of hardware and help us get that execution right.” Sourcing components could also be a challenge. Though Runware says it designs and builds its own cooling and other pod systems with standard components, some parts, such as pumps and fans, come from Germany, and it still depends on Nvidia for networking. Still, Runware claims it has received $1 billion in committed interest for its Sonic pods since it began offering them to outside customers a month ago, “representing over 20 megawatts, which we’re now working to deliver,” Radulescu said. Data centers in the U.S. and abroad have come under fire for how much energy they consume and how that affects the grid and other resources. When pressed, Radulescu said his company’s pods only need power and an internet connection. They’ll use a closed-loop liquid cooling system with air-cooled radiators to release heat, so they don’t really need a water connection. “We’re working with power providers on a site pipeline covering 397 megawatts, with potential to expand to 1.2 gigawatts,” he said, referring to its list of planned sites and adding that the company is deploying its modular data centers on sites that are much smaller than those used by hyperscalers like Amazon, Microsoft, and Google. The sites, he continued, typically already have power, so they shouldn’t further strain the grid or disrupt the community. The pods also run “completely silent up to temperatures of 86 degrees Fahrenheit. We use energy from renewable sources whenever possible,” he continued. “We are actively working on expanding our network of energy providers and sites. We’re aiming to have renewables as our main energy source.”

articles.title: Waymo taps Toyota to supply robotaxis for Japan and the U.K. | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Waymo will begin testing self-driving versions of Toyota's electric bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker.
articles.body_text: Waymo will begin testing autonomous Toyota bZ4X vehicles in Japan next year as part of a broader partnership with the automaker to provide electric vehicles for robotaxi operations in international markets, including the U.K. Under the partnership announced Friday, Toyota will manufacture the 2027 bZ4X vehicles and integrate Waymo’s self-driving system at its Takaoka factory in Japan. (The electric vehicle is now known as the BZ in the North American market) The autonomous bZ4X vehicles will initially be tested in Japan, where Waymo intends to eventually operate a robotaxi service. But the intent is to deploy these vehicles in other right-hand driving countries such as the U.K. Waymo has been testing its autonomous Jaguar I-Pace vehicles in London for months and plans to launch a robotaxi service there once it receives the necessary permits. The announcement comes 18 months after Toyota and Waymo signed a preliminary agreement to explore the development and deployment of an autonomous vehicle platform. At the time, the agreement fell into the “let’s see what happens” category, with language vague enough to leave plenty of room for interpretation. For now, the partnership looks more like a conventional vehicle supplier deal that helps Waymo fill specific regional needs while adding a new model to its robotaxi portfolio. But the partnership could go beyond robotaxis. The companies said they will continue to look at bringing Waymo’s autonomous technology to personally owned Toyota vehicles. Toyota and Waymo also announced plans to look at other future “initiatives” that would use “insights from Waymo’s real-world operations” to improve safety for other road users. What that might mean is unclear, although Hiroki Nakajima, executive vice president of Toyota and a board member, provided some clues. “This collaboration will help scale that technology and bring it to customers in Japan and beyond through Waymo’s ride-hailing service, and in parallel, Toyota will continue to explore how integrating vehicles with traffic infrastructure can make those roads safer still,” he said in a statement. But coming off the blockbuster success of this year’s hit movie “Project Hail Mary,” Hollywood has become a lucrative business for the e-commerce giant. Prime Video, Amazon’s streaming service, “has emerged as a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars and is now profitable in its own right,” Amazon CEO Andy Jassy said on the quarterly earnings call on Thursday. Jassy had previously told investors in May that Prime Video was profitable , but being on track to generate tens of billions is a new detail. articles.title: As search traffic dries up, Reddit announces it's shifting to a logged-in experience | TechCrunch
articles.summary: As AI transforms how people find information online, Reddit is rethinking its open-web roots to protect its audience and business.
articles.body_text: Reddit has long attracted millions of users to its site through Google, with many even appending the word “Reddit” to their search queries for better answers. But as search traffic dries up amid the shift to AI-powered search, Reddit is rethinking its relationship with the open internet. In its third-quarter earnings call on Thursday, the company announced it’s transitioning to a primarily “logged-in experience.” The move is designed to protect its data from AI scraping, allowing the company to instead forge lucrative licensing deals with model providers. But just as important, such a shift could help Reddit to increase its revenue even as it faces daily active user declines in its largest market, the U.S. Overall, Reddit’s global daily active users were flat quarter-over-quarter in Q3, reaching 130.3 million, while U.S. daily active users dropped from 53.2 million in Q2 to 50.7 million in Q3 and were down 2% year-over-year. The company is not alone in seeing such declines; the shift to an AI-centered web has impacted most websites and publishers by now, leading to fewer click-throughs, as AI summaries provide answers that don’t require website visits and Google’s traditional “ten blue links” have reduced relevance. (The change is now even impacting Google’s bottom line , its earnings revealed.) But at Reddit’s scale, the numbers associated with such a decline are enormous. The company said search traffic referrals dropped by more than 1 million referrals on average per week in October. It warned that if the trend continues, daily active users could decline to a low-double-digit percentage by next quarter. (To play that out: a hypothetical 10% to 12% decline could bring Reddit to roughly 115 million to 117 million daily actives, down from 130.3 million in Q3. That’s a huge drop!) At the same time, Reddit has gotten significantly better at monetizing its audience even as its growth weakens. Revenue increased 53% year-over-year to $895 million, ahead of Wall Street’s expectations of about $875 million. Net income rose 74% to $283 million. Advertising revenue grew 54% to $847 million while nonadvertising revenue, which includes its AI data-licensing business, grew 35% year-over-year to $48 million. And despite a 2% year-over-year decline in U.S. daily users, Reddit’s average revenue per daily active user in the U.S. rose 53% to $13.82. Globally, average revenue per daily active user increased 36% year-over-year to $6.87. Shifting to a logged-in experience could boost those numbers even higher because logged-in users are typically worth more to advertisers. Unlike the logged-out users who often find their way to the site via search, logged-in users provide more signals about their interests and behaviors, which helps to better target and personalize ads. Still, a change of this magnitude could be the canary in the coal mine for the open web. “I don’t know about you, but as someone whose life has been defined by the open internet, it’s a big change for me,” wrote Reddit co-founder and CEO Steve Huffman in a post published on Reddit’s site . “But I’ve come to the conclusion that this is the right decision for our platform and the right decision for our business,” he said. The company notes that the shift to the logged-in experience will not be an overnight change; it will first run tests in select markets outside the U.S. in the fourth quarter. It doesn’t yet have a timeline for when the change will be rolled out to all its users worldwide. It also acknowledged that access to a logged-out front page is important.

articles.title: The R2 SUV is already Rivian's best-selling vehicle | TechCrunch
articles.summary: Rivian is seeing strong enough sales of the new EV that it improved its guidance to Wall Street for the second time this year.
articles.body_text: Rivian’s new R2 SUV was its best-selling vehicle in the third quarter, the company said Thursday, marking an auspicious start for the all-important EV. While Rivian didn’t say exactly how many R2s it sold over the three-month period, the company is confident enough in the pace of sales that it raised its delivery guidance for Wall Street. Rivian had previously expected to deliver between 65,000 and 70,000 EVs this year. On Thursday, it bumped up that floor to 67,000. It’s the second time Rivian has raised its delivery guidance this year, and the company is now on track to break a three-year stalemate during which it struggled to ship more than 50,000 vehicles annually. The company launched the R2 just in June, but it has made a major bet on scaling production of the lower-cost SUV at a historically quick rate. The early success of the R2 is also a sign that Rivian is finding new customers despite last year’s loss of the $7,500 federal EV tax credit. The death of that tax credit, along with changes made by the Trump administration to U.S. regulations that supported the growth of EVs, has caused many major automakers to shift their attention back to internal combustion and hybrid vehicles — leaving room in the market for pure-EV companies like Tesla and Rivian. “In a U.S. automotive marketplace starved for high-quality EV choice, R2 is an attractively priced option for everyday adventures that is resonating with a broad set of consumers and we expect will be a game changer for Rivian’s long-term growth and profitability,” the company said in a letter to shareholders released Thursday. Rivian revealed earlier this month that it built 19,751 vehicles in the third quarter and delivered 19,248. That was roughly 45% more than it delivered in the same period last year and a big jump from the 12,613 vehicles built and 12,194 delivered in the second quarter of 2026. The increase was driven in large part by the company launching a second production shift at its factory in Normal, Illinois. Rivian said Thursday that the R2 was responsible for “much of the gain quarter-over-quarter,” but didn’t go into specifics. The company generated $2.2 billion in revenue in the third quarter and suffered a net loss of $913 million — down from $1.2 billion in the same period last year. Rivian launched the R2 at a starting price of just under $60,000. A more affordable “premium” trim is supposed to be available later this year that starts at $53,990. articles.title: Bluesky blocks links to leaked DHS employee data as government seeks takedowns | TechCrunch
articles.summary: The social networking site is facing criticism for blocking access to the site, which identifies thousands of ICE agents and other employees working for Homeland Security.
articles.body_text: Following a sizable leak of personnel data about employees who work for the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, social network Bluesky is now blocking its users from accessing a nonprofit’s website that hosts the leaked dataset. Users reported that the links to nonprofit transparency collective DDoSecrets were marked as “malicious” soon after TechCrunch and other media outlets broke the news that Homeland Security had been hacked. TechCrunch reported on Wednesday that a hacker obtained over 40,000 user account records from Homeland Security’s login system, including the names and contact information, such as work-issued phone numbers and email addresses, of employees and agents working for its various agencies like Customs and Border Protection (CBP) and Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE). The data included information that was similar to that on an employee’s business card. DDoSecrets, which publishes leaked datasets in the public interest, also made the hacked data publicly available. Researchers who are investigating abuses by the Trump administration say that the data will be invaluable for seeking records from the government under public records laws. A spokesperson for Homeland Security told TechCrunch on Wednesday that it was “aware of a potential breach and is actively working to address the situation swiftly and effectively.” “When deciding between blocking a link and removing individual posts, we chose to block the links to avoid limiting public discussion or restricting broader access to reporting and commentary,” said Wang. In a post on Bluesky, Wang said that the company plans to change the wording on the block message. “We should have changed the wording last night. Changes incoming shortly,” said Wang. DDoSecrets co-founder and journalist Emma Best told TechCrunch that while Bluesky’s terms of service prohibit sharing home addresses and personal contact information, Best said that neither of these is in the leaked dataset. “The data contains professional contact information for government employees at a time when the public interest in that exact information has never been higher. By requiring the public to provide it for [Freedom of Information Act] requests, the government has made that exact information a crucial piece of the transparency channels they want the public to engage in,” said Best. Best told TechCrunch that a website hosting a searchable copy of the stolen data was taken down by its domain registrar, effectively knocking the website offline for now. A search site , dubbed Icepick, made by journalist maia arson crimew no longer loads as of Thursday morning. An internet record associated with the domain says it has been placed on “serverHold,” which generally means that the domain registrar locked or closed the domain for some reason. Homeland Security filed a takedown notice via a security vendor called ZeroFox, which has authority to act on the department’s behalf until 2028 to seek the removal of data from the internet. TechCrunch has seen a copy of the takedown notice for the search site, which asks that the domain registrar “stop serving the personal contact and location data of individuals who did not consent to its publication.”

articles.title: Google’s new Jules AI agent will help developers fix buggy code
articles.summary: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that uses Gemini 2.0 to automatically fix Python and Javascript coding errors.
articles.body_text: Google has announced an experimental AI-powered code agent called “Jules” that can automatically fix coding errors for developers. Jules was introduced today alongside Gemini 2.0, and uses the updated Google AI model to create multi-step plans to address issues, modify multiple files, and prepare pull requests for Python and Javascript coding tasks in GitHub workflows. Microsoft introduced a similar experience for GitHub Copilot last year that can recognize and explain code, alongside recommending changes and fixing bugs. Jules will compete against Microsoft’s offering, and also against tools like Cursor and even Claude and ChatGPT’s coding abilities. Google’s launch of a coding-focused AI assistant is no surprise — CEO Sundar Pichai said in October that more than a quarter of all new code at the company is now generated by AI. “Jules handles bug fixes and other time-consuming tasks while you focus on what you actually want to build,” Google says in its blog post. “This effort is part of our long-term goal of building AI agents that are helpful in all domains, including coding.” Developers have full control to review and adjust the plans created by Jules, before choosing to merge the code it generates into their projects. The announcement doesn’t say that Jules will spot bugs for you, so presumably it needs to be directed to a list of issues that have already been identified to fix. Google also says that Jules is in early development and “may make mistakes,” but internal testing has shown it’s been beneficial for boosting developer productivity and providing real-time updates to help track and manage tasks. Jules is launching today for a “select group of trusted testers” according to Google, and will be released to other developers in early 2025. Updates about availability and how development is progressing will be available via the Google Labs website.

articles.title: Harley-Davidson spins out LiveWire as its own electric motorcycle brand
articles.summary: Harley-Davidson is spinning out its electric motorcycle division as a standalone company called LiveWire. A new electrified model will be unveiled in July.
articles.body_text: LiveWire, the first electric motorcycle from Harley-Davidson, will now become its own standalone brand. The Milwaukee-based company announced that it would be spinning out its electric motorcycle division as its own company with a distinct lineup and a tailored retail experience. Harley-Davidson plans to unveil the “first LiveWire branded motorcycle” on July 8th to coincide with the International Motorcycle Show. It’s a similar move to how Harley-Davidson approached its new electric bicycle company, Serial 1. The idea is that LiveWire continues to benefit from its relationship with its parent company while also forging its own brand identity that is distinct from Harley-Davidson. It’s a shift from how the company approached its current LiveWire model, in which the Harley-Davidson logo is front and center, while the LiveWire brand is practically nonexistent. And it’s a sign that going forward, Harley-Davidson is interested in letting its electrified models stand on their own terms. “With the mission to be the most desirable electric motorcycle brand in the world, LiveWire will pioneer the future of motorcycling, for the pursuit of urban adventure and beyond,” Jochen Zeitz, chairman, president, and CEO of Harley-Davidson, said in a statement. “LiveWire also plans to innovate and develop technology that will be applicable to Harley-Davidson electric motorcycles in the future.” [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/22504479/3_LiveWire_Black_CMYK_PRIMARY_LOCKUP.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] There’s a new logo and a new “virtual” headquarters, with engineering teams stationed in Silicon Valley and Milwaukee. LiveWire will work with Harley-Davidson dealerships as an independent brand, with a blend of digital and physical retail formats. Asked whether this will include online ordering, a Harley-Davidson spokesperson responded with a cautiously worded statement. “It depends on the state in which you live,” the spokesperson said. “LiveWire is creating a purchase path that allows us to meet the expectations for a digital-first purchase experience, supported by a network of committed dealers that allow customers to choose their path and engagement model.” The question is whether this branding strategy will lead to better sales for Harley-Davidson’s electric models. Last year, Reuters reported that the company’s plan to appeal to a younger generation of motorcyclists with the LiveWire was struggling, with most of the preorders coming from older or preexisting customers. Harley-Davidson’s overall sales have been stagnant lately after hitting a low point in 2018. The problem could be that the price, which starts at $29,799, isn’t that much cheaper than a Tesla Model 3. Dealers told Reuters that many younger customers were turned off by the price tag. Harley-Davidson is also facing some stiff competition from rivals like Zero Motorcycles, which recently teamed up with power sports manufacturer Polaris on a new lineup of electric-powered ATVs and snowmobiles. And as the broader world of transportation shifts to electric, the company will be under increasing pressure from its shareholders to prove its vision for the future can be profitable.

articles.title: The Nvidia AI antitrust investigation is ‘escalating,’ reports Bloomberg
articles.summary: Nvidia and other companies have received subpoenas indicating a Department of Justice antitrust investigation into its AI chip business is moving forward.
articles.body_text: An antitrust investigation by the Department of Justice focusing on Nvidia’s AI dominance as the hardware company of choice is escalating, reports Bloomberg. The outlet reports that Nvidia and other companies have received legally binding requests for information as its sources say regulators are investigating whether Nvidia is “making it harder to switch to other suppliers and penalizes buyers that don’t exclusively use its artificial intelligence chips.” “Nvidia wins on merit, as reflected in our benchmark results and value to customers, and customers can choose whatever solution is best for them. We have inquired with the U.S. Department of Justice and have not been subpoenaed. Nonetheless, we are happy to answer any questions regulators may have about our business,” said Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo, as reported previously by CNBC. Earlier this summer, Nvidia had overtaken Microsoft as the world’s most valuable company, but now it trails both Microsoft and Apple. Before the subpoenas were reported on Tuesday afternoon, its share price dropped more than 9 percent, wiping out about $279 billion in market value in one day. But as Bloomberg notes, Nvidia’s stock is still up more than double this year as the AI boom has fueled sales of the company’s pricey chips, even after a report by The Information a few weeks ago saying that its upcoming Blackwell series of AI chips may be delayed “by three months or more due to design flaws.” Update, September 4th: Added Nvidia statement previously reported by CNBC.

articles.title: How AI companies are reckoning with elections
articles.summary: AI could play a prominent role in the 2024 US presidential election, and the companies behind it have each said how they plan to make sure their impact isn’t disastrous.
articles.body_text: The US is heading into its first presidential election since generative AI tools have gone mainstream. And the companies offering these tools — like Google, OpenAI, and Microsoft — have each made announcements about how they plan to handle the months leading up to it. This election season, we’ve already seen AI-generated images in ads and attempts to mislead voters with voice cloning. The potential harms from AI chatbots aren’t as visible in the public eye — yet, anyway. But chatbots are known to confidently provide made-up facts, including in responses to good-faith questions about basic voting information. In a high-stakes election, that could be disastrous. One plausible solution is to try to avoid election-related queries altogether. In December, Google announced that Gemini would simply refuse to answer election-related questions in the US, referring users to Google Search instead. Google spokesperson Christa Muldoon confirmed to The Verge via email the change is now rolling out globally. (Of course, that relies on the reliability of Google Search — something the company has been working on with an eye toward AI spam.) Muldoon said Google has “no plans” to lift these restrictions, which she said also “apply to all queries and outputs” generated by Gemini, not just text. Earlier this year, OpenAI said that ChatGPT would start referring users to CanIVote.org, generally considered one of the best online resources for local voting information. The company’s policy now forbids impersonating candidates or local governments using ChatGPT. It likewise prohibits using its tools for campaigning, lobbying, discouraging voting, or otherwise misrepresenting the voting process, under the updated rules. In a statement emailed to The Verge, Aravind Srinivas, CEO of the AI search company Perplexity, said Perplexity’s algorithms prioritize “reliable and reputable sources like news outlets” and that it always provides links so users can verify its output. In an email to The Verge, Microsoft representative Brian Gluckman says the company has rolled out updates to address concerns from a report last year about false election information provided by Copilot (formerly known as Bing). His email also pointed to the company’s blog post about combating abusive AI content as an example of the measures it’s applying, with provenance technology, bans for users who break the rules, and more. All of these companies’ responses (maybe Google’s most of all) are very different from how they’ve tended to approach elections with their other products. Google has used (and continues to use) Associated Press partnerships to bring factual election information to the top of search results and has tried to counter false claims about mail-in voting by using labels on YouTube. Other companies have made similar efforts — see Facebook’s voter registration links and Twitter’s anti-misinformation banner. Yet major events like the US presidential election seem like a real opportunity to prove whether AI chatbots are actually a useful shortcut to legitimate information. I asked a couple of Texas voting questions of some chatbots to get an idea of their usefulness. OpenAI’s ChatGPT 4 was able to correctly list the seven different forms of valid ID for voters, and it also identified that the next significant election is the primary runoff election on May 28th. Perplexity AI answered those questions correctly as well, linking multiple sources at the top. Copilot got its answers right and even did one better by telling me what my options were if I didn’t have any of the seven forms of ID. (ChatGPT also coughed up this addendum on a second try). Gemini just referred me to Google Search, which got me the right answers about ID, but when I asked for the date of next election, an out-of-date box at the top referred me to the March 5th primary. Many of the companies working on AI have made various commitments to prevent or mitigate the intentional misuse of their products. Microsoft says it will work with candidates and political parties to curtail election misinformation. The company has also started releasing what it says will be regular reports on foreign influences in key elections — its first such threat analysis came in November. Google says it will digitally watermark images created with its products using DeepMind’s SynthID. OpenAI and Microsoft have both announced that they would use the Coalition for Content Provenance and Authenticity’s (C2PA) digital credentials to denote AI-generated images with a CR symbol. But each company has said that these approaches aren’t enough. One way Microsoft plans to account for that is through its website that lets political candidates report deepfakes. Stability AI, which owns the Stable Diffusion image generator, updated its policies recently to ban using its product for “fraud or the creation or promotion of disinformation.” Midjourney told Reuters last week that “updates related specifically to the upcoming U.S. election are coming soon.” Its image generator performed the worst when it came to making misleading images, according to a Center for Countering Digital Hate report published last week. Meta announced in November of last year that it would require political advertisers to disclose if they used “AI or other digital techniques” to create ads published on its platforms. The company has also banned the use of its generative AI tools by political campaigns and groups. [Image: The “Seven Principle Goals” of the AI Elections accord. https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/25332126/Screenshot_2024_03_12_at_11.21.50_AM.png?quality=90&strip=all] Several companies, including all of the ones above, signed an accord last month, promising to create new ways to mitigate the deceptive use of AI in elections. The companies agreed on seven “principle goals,” like research and deployment of prevention methods, giving provenance for content (such as with C2PA or SynthID-style watermarking), improving their AI detection capabilities, and collectively evaluating and learning from the effects of misleading AI-generated content. In January, two companies in Texas cloned President Biden’s voice to discourage voting in the New Hampshire primary. It won’t be the last time generative AI makes an unwanted appearance in this election cycle. As the 2024 race heats up, we’ll surely see these companies tested on the safeguards they’ve built and the commitments they’ve made. articles.title: Inside Facebook’s election war room
articles.summary: In a Menlo Park conference room, a global effort to fight misinformation comes together
articles.body_text: Information war, meet the war room. Facebook on Wednesday briefed reporters on its latest efforts to uncover nefarious uses of the platform during election season, offering a tour of the large conference room where dozens of employees are monitoring events around the clock. “We know when it comes to an elections, every moment counts,” said Samidh Chakrabarti, head of civic engagement at Facebook, who oversees the war room. “So if there are late-breaking issues we see on the platform, we need to be able to detect and respond to them in real time, as quickly as possible.” On one hand, the war room is just one of many conference rooms in MPK 20, the company’s Menlo Park, CA headquarters. But it’s larger than average, and has been stuffed with people and electronics equipment. There are desks for 24 people, and the room is ringed with 17 screens, each of which highlights a different stream of information Facebook is monitoring. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289699/T6B3ly8w.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] Employees look for suspicious spikes in spam and hate speech, in some cases using custom software built for the purpose. They look for efforts at voter suppression, such as falsely telling people that lines are long or that the election has been delayed. (The team recently uncovered one such hoax claiming that the Brazilian election date had been delayed a day due to protests, and swiftly removed the offending posts.) Sign up for The Interface Get The Verge’s daily newsletter about social networks and democracy the night before everyone else does. Sign up Other employees use CrowdTangle, a company acquired by Facebook that monitors the viral spread of articles across platforms, to detect which articles are trending on Facebook, Instagram, Twitter, and Reddit. All told, representatives from 20 teams have people in the war room, representing 20,000 global employees working on safety and security. The teams include threat intelligence, data science, engineering, research, operations, legal, policy, communications, and representatives from Facebook-owned WhatsApp and Instagram. [Image: https://platform.theverge.com/wp-content/uploads/sites/2/chorus/uploads/chorus_asset/file/13289701/ygMhHSnw.jpg?quality=90&strip=all] If anyone finds a problem, they escalate it to a specialist, who can then route it to the appropriate decision-maker. Facebook has also given state attorneys general and other elected officials a way to reach the war room quickly to report voter suppression and other suspicious activity. If the room is new, the work is not: Facebook teams have been working to fight misinformation in a coordinated way since 2016. The decision to bring them all together into a single room was made in the hopes that it would let them make decisions faster. “When every moment counts, then decision-making needs to be fast,” Chakrabarti sayd. “There’s no substitute for face to face, in-room interaction. so we felt [the need for] this physical war room to be able to coordinate teams.” On the day we visited, the room was decorated with a mix of American and Brazilian flags, in a nod to the next two elections that are being watched in the war room. It’s a fraught time: last week, Facebook removed 559 pages and 251 accounts in the United States for using fake identities and coordinating information campaigns. Meanwhile, Brazilian researchers today published the results of a study that examined the most-shared images in popular public WhatsApp chats and found that many of them contained misinformation: > From a sample of more than 100,000 political images that circulated in those 347 groups, we selected the 50 most widely shared. They were reviewed by Agência Lupa, which is Brazil’s leading fact-checking platform. Eight of those 50 photos and images were considered completely false; 16 were real pictures but used out of their original context or related to distorted data; four were unsubstantiated claims, not based on a trustworthy public source. This means that 56 percent of the most-shared images were misleading. Only 8 percent of the 50 most widely shared images were considered fully truthful. Facebook wouldn’t commit to keeping the war room open over forever. But with multiple elections taking place around the world each year, the company plans to keep it open for the foreseeable future. “This is going to be a constant arms race,” said Katie Harbath, Facebook’s global politics and government outreach director. “This is our new normal. Bad actors are going to get more sophisticated in what they’re doing, and we’re going to have to get more sophisticated in trying to catch them.”

articles.title: Påven har röstat i amerikanska valet: ”Utövat sin rösträtt”
articles.summary: Påve Leo XIV är den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val. ”Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande.
articles.body_text: Påve Leo XIV är den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val. ” Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer ”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. 3 november är det mellanårsval i USA. Nu har den katolska kyrkans ledare, påve Leo XIV, blivit den första påven i historien att rösta i ett amerikanskt val, skriver Chicago Sun Times. ” Påven Leo XIV har utövat sin rösträtt som amerikansk medborgare, närhelst han varit berättigad att göra det ”, skriver Heliga stolen i ett pressmeddelande. Enligt Heliga stolens presskontor brukar påven använda sin rösträtt när han har rätt och möjlighet att göra det. Bland annat när han arbetade för den katolska kyrkan i Peru. ” Den heliga fadern uttrycker sin tro på medborgarnas rätt och skyldighet att delta i demokratiska processer ”, skriver de i uttalandet. Påven har flera gånger kritiserat USA:s president Donald Trump för att bedriva en dålig utrikes- och migrationspolitik. Bland annat har han anklagat Trump för att ha ett storhetsvansinne. Det har fått den amerikanska presidenten att se rött. På Truth social har han tidigare anklagat påven för att vara ”usel” på utrikespolitik och svag på brottsbekämpning. – Jag är inte ett fan av påve Leo, har Trump sagt till reportrar. Utspelet kom efter ett inlägg på Truth Social om påven. ” Jag vill inte ha en påve som tycker det är okej för Iran att ha kärnvapen. Jag vill inte ha en påve som tycker det är hemskt att USA attackerade Venezuela. ”, skrev Trump i april.

articles.title: Svensken: ”Är skurken i den här historien”
articles.summary: Kryssningsföretaget tiggde enorma summor pengar från sina passagerare – men i veckan blev det tvärstopp och 200 passagerare är strandsatta i Kambodja.
articles.body_text: Kryssningsföretaget tiggde enorma summor pengar från sina passagerare – men i veckan blev det tvärstopp och 200 passagerare är strandsatta i Kambodja. Svensken Mikael Petterson ligger bakom företaget. – Jag är skurken i den här historien, säger han till Business Insider . Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Lyxfartyget ”The Odyssey” har den senaste tiden skapat rubriker över hela världen. Fartygets 203 passagerare är nu strandsatta i Kambodja efter ett halvår som har kantats av en stadigt sjunkande kvalitet ombord. – Jag är skurken i den här historien, men jag gör allt jag kan för att stötta de boende med en lösning, säger svensken Mikael Petterson, grundare av det ansvariga företaget Villa Vie Residences, till Business Insider. Samtidigt som internetuppkopplingen och maten rapporteras ha blivit sämre har kryssningsföretaget pressat de boende på pengar för att hålla sig självt flytande. Amerikanska pensionärsparet Lynn, 64, och Paul Montoya, 68, hade redan betalat 1,8 miljoner kronor för sin hytt, rapporterar Daily Mail. Nu har de pungat ut med totalt 4,4 miljoner kronor för vad som skulle bli en flerårig drömresa. Villa Vie Residences affärsidé var att hyra ut ”flytande hem” på fartyget ”The Odyssey”. Hytterna hyrdes ut i avtal som löpte över fem år eller längre men kunde också köpas som permanentbostäder.

articles.title: Paulina kan sova i ett dygn – är ändå alltid trött
articles.summary: Om Paulina Johansson Merkell, 34, sover i åtta timmar känns det som att hon inte har sovit på flera dagar. Så har det varit sedan hon fick den ovanliga sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni.
articles.body_text: Paulina Johansson Merkell, 34, kan ha sovit i åtta timmar – ändå känns det som att hon varit vaken i flera dygn. Hon lider av den ovanliga sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni. – Jag levde livet och sen bara ”pang” så var jag sängbunden nästan, säger hon. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Efter gymnasiet levde Paulina Johansson Merkell från Uppsala som en vanlig ung vuxen. Hon reste mycket, festade med vänner, skaffade ett heltidsjobb och hade planer på att börja studera. Men när hon inte orkade lika mycket som vännerna, somnade på jobbet och ständigt mådde dåligt förstod hon att någonting inte stod rätt till, vilket hon tidigare har berättat om för SVT Uppsala . Läkare tyckte hon var för ung för att vara så pass trött – och proverna visade ingenting avvikande – men efter många vårdrundor fick hon som 23-åring en diagnos: Den kroniska sömnsjukdomen idiopatisk hypersomni. – Det var jättejobbigt. Alla ens kompisar och släkt levde vidare sina liv och jag var fast hemma och sov. Jag fick lägga om hela mitt liv och allting som jag hade tänkt för min framtid, säger hon. Idiopatisk hypersomni är en mycket ovanlig diagnos och innebär att man lider av extrem sömnighet på dagtid, trots att man sover normalt eller extra mycket, enligt Läkemedelsboken. Innan Paulina blev sjukskriven var arbetsdagarna plågsamma och till slut blev hon av med jobbet. – Jag ville inte aktivt ta mitt liv, men jag kände om det skulle hända någonting, om jag skulle dö, så skulle det inte göra någonting för då skulle jag slippa vara vaken. Som längst har hon sovit i 31 timmar i sträck, med undantag för korta vakna stunder för att äta något och gå på toa. En vanlig dag blir det 12-18 timmars sömn.

articles.title: Svensk forskare förbjuds resa in
articles.summary: Svenske forskaren och författaren Andreas Malm, 49, portas från att resa till Storbritannien.
articles.body_text: Svenske forskaren och författaren Andreas Malm, 49, portas från att resa till Storbritannien. – Jag blev ganska chockad, säger han till Expressen. Malm skulle medverka i ett arrangemang tillsammans med grundaren för den i landet terrorstämplade gruppen Palestine Action. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Andreas Malm, författare och humanekolog, har nekats inresa till Storbritannien, rapporterar The Guardian . Den brittiska immigrationsmyndigheten har nu nekat honom inresa eftersom hans närvaro ”kanske inte kan vara till gagn för allmänhetens bästa”. I onsdags fick Malm, docent vid institutionen för kulturgeografi och ekonomisk geografi vid Lunds universitet, ett mejl med beskedet. – Jag blev ganska chockad. Det borde jag kanske inte ha blivit. Men jag har åkt hur mycket som helst till Storbritannien i decennier, jag var där senast i maj och talade under en festival, säger Andreas Malm. Malm skulle under nästa vecka ha talat vid en konferens i London kallad ”Washingtons globala terrorvälde och Storbritanniens roll i att tvinga igenom det”. – Jag skulle tala om hur jakten på fossila bränslen är en del av de amerikanska krigen i Venezuela, Iran och övriga Mellanöstern, säger Malm. Malms tal skulle hållas tillsammans med Huda Ammori, en av medgrundarna till den i landet terrorstämplade organisationen Palestine Action. Storbritannien förbjöd Palestine Action i juli 2025 under landets terrorlagstiftning och det är även olagligt att uttrycka stöd för organisationen.

articles.title: Väljarna som sviker Trump: ”Ångrar mig”
articles.summary: De slöt upp bakom Trump i presidentvalet, till somligas förvåning. Men nu har många latinos i Texas fått nog. – Med tanke på allt som har hänt ångrar jag att jag röstade på honom, säger predikanten Cassandra Sarmiento.
articles.body_text: De slöt upp bakom Trump i presidentvalet, till somligas förvåning. Men nu har många latinos i Texas fått nog. – Med tanke på allt som har hänt ångrar jag att jag röstade på honom, säger predikanten Cassandra Sarmiento. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. De är tejanos, för att vara exakt. Ordet är spanskans motsvarighet till engelskans Texans (alltså ett uttryck för personer från Texas), men det spanska ordet syftar på de Texasbor som har mexikanskt ursprung. Tejano är också en en musikstil som hör hemma här vid gränsen mellan Mexiko och Texas. Den har mexikanska gitarrer men också stompiga dragspel, som kommer från tyskarna och tjeckerna som hamnade i Texas i drivor och tog med sig sin polka. Bobby Pulido har varit en av genrens stora stjärnor sedan 90-talet, när han slog igenom med ”Desvelado”, en smäktande ballad om en man som inte kan sova för han är så förälskad i en kvinna. Han har aldrig träffat henne, bara fastnat för hennes röst på radion. Nu är det andra röster som Pulido jagar. Han har nämligen sadlat om från tejanostjärna till demokratisk kandidat till representanthuset i Texas 15:e distrikt. Så det är kanske inte för mycket att gissa att han inte får så mycket sömn nu heller, de här sista nätterna inför valet. Det femtonde distriktet går som ett vingligt Jengatorn genom södra Texas, med start öster om San Antonio, och ner hela vägen till gränsen mot Mexiko. Här ner mot Rio Grande-dalgången gick Donald Trump från klarhet till klarhet i de senaste presidentvalen. 2016 förlorade han klart mot Clinton, 2020 vann han snävt mot Biden och för två år sen var det en kross med 17 procentenheter över Kamala Harris. Men efter snart en halv mandatperiod knakar det betänkligt i relationen mellan Trump och väljarna här. Pulido leder mot republikanen Monica de la Cruz, enligt mätningarna, trots att republikanerna har ritat om distriktskartan för att gynna sina kandidater. På ett nöjesfält i McAllen, en av gränsstäderna i distriktet, går folk omkring i neonljuset, käkar popcorn och håller ordning på uppspelta barn som springer ut från karusellerna.

articles.title: Vädjar till V – att släppa kravet: ”Offrar maktskifte”
articles.summary: Cuf-toppens krav på Andersson
articles.body_text: Cuf-ledaren Emelie Rossheim vädjar till Vänsterpartiet att släppa regeringskravet. Annars kommer den rödgröna ”soppan” inte att lösa sig, varnar hon. – Är V villiga att offra medmänsklig politik och ett maktskifte? Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Att V och C bråkar offentligt skadar den rödgröna regeringsbildningen – och det är framför allt Socialdemokraternas fel. Det tycker Emelie Rossheim, ordförande för Centerpartiets ungdomsförbund. Nu måste Magdalena Andersson klargöra om hon vill se Vänsterpartiet i regering eller inte, säger den 27-åriga Cuf-basen som väntas bli omvald i helgen. – Annars kommer vi inte att komma vidare. Emelie Rossheim kallar Vänsterpartiets regeringskrav för ”djupt oansvarigt”. – Det är utomordentligt korkat att Vänsterpartiet vill tvinga Centerpartiet att välja sida, när vi redan har uppvisat just den här enorma samarbetsviljan. För utan C blir det inget regeringsskifte. Och den här soppan kommer inte lösa sig om inte V ändrar sig. Då kommer att dröja flera år innan vi har en rödgrön majoritet. Enligt Rossheim finns det flera områden där de rödgröna kan göra gemensam sak. Hon nämner bland annat jobben, småföretagande, klimatet samt en stark röst för demokrati och mänskliga rättigheter i världen. Hon ifrågasätter hur långt Vänsterpartiet kan gå för att få ministerposter.

articles.title: Nya C-strategin: Pressar S om ett regeringsbesked • ”Kommer för billigt undan”
articles.summary: Regeringsbildningen går trögt. Nu måste Socialdemokraterna ge besked om vilka de vill bilda regering med, menar Centerpartiets ledning. – Det är naturligt att Centerpartiet höjer insatserna på sin sida litegrann och markerar att regeringsbildningen är Socialdemokraternas ansvar, säger statsvetaren Andreas Johansson Heinö.
articles.body_text: Nu måste Socialdemokraterna ge besked om vilka de vill bilda regering med, menar Centerpartiets ledning. – Det är naturligt att Centerpartiet höjer insatserna på sin sida litegrann och markerar att regeringsbildningen är Socialdemokraternas ansvar, säger statsvetaren Andreas Johansson Heinö. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. De rödgröna partierna har ännu inte kommit i gång med regeringsförhandlingar. Vänsterpartiets och Centerpartiets oförenliga linjer gör läget låst. Socialdemokraterna har efter valet inte sagt vilka partier man vill regera med. Magdalena Andersson har heller inte velat berätta det för talman Andreas Norlén. – Nej, det har hon inte gjort. Hon har inte resonerat om det som efterfrågas offentligt, sa han till Expressen på torsdagseftermiddagen. Vänsterpartiet har tidigare önskat ett tydligt besked från Socialdemokraterna om att de ska få ingå i regeringen. Nu är Centerpartiet inne på samma spår. Partiets ekonomisk-politiska talesperson Martin Ådahl menar att Vänsterpartiet har ”falska förhoppningar” om att få ministerposter. – Vi tänker oss att man är lika tydlig efter valet som före med att V inte är redo för att sitta i regering. Då blir det lättare att komma framåt. Och det är inget som går att hänskjuta till C eller någon annan. Just nu så riskerar många att kanske leva på väldigt falska förhoppningar, sa han till Svenska Dagbladet häromdagen. Nu säger Centerpartiets ledare Elisabeth Thand Ringqvist samma sak. I en kommentar om talmannens beslut att låta riksdagen rösta om henne som statsminister – trots att hon sonderade möjligheten att bilda en ”mittenregering” som skulle ledas av Magdalena Andersson – skriver hon: ”Det finns fortfarande behov av större tydlighet kring vilka regeringsalternativ inte minst Socialdemokraterna är beredda att medverka till”. Enligt uppgifter till Expressen finns en irritation mot Socialdemokraterna inom Centerpartiet. En källa i partiet beskriver situationen som ”bisarr”.

articles.body_text: 71 danska skattemiljoner som skulle ha gått till granater åt Ukraina hamnade i stället hos ett italienskt företag som aldrig tillverkat granater, skriver Danwatch. Ljuduppspelningen är AI-genererad. Felaktigheter kan förekomma. Pengarna ingår i ett stort stödpaket, värt totalt över 300 miljoner danska kronor, som Danmarks regering presenterade i april i fjol. Donationen gjordes via Estland. Enligt estländska medier lades snabbt 71 miljoner danska kronor (motsvarande drygt 100 miljoner svenska) på beställningar av granater. Men Ukraina har inte fått en enda granat. Pengarna gick till en italiensk mjukvaruutvecklare som 2024 köptes av företag i Indien. Inget av företagen har någonsin tillverkat artillerigranater, men vägrar betala tillbaka några pengar, skriver Danwatch . I september avgick Estlands dåvarande försvarsminister Hanno Pevkur på grund av affären. I Danmark växer kraven på en utredning. Detta är en nyhetsartikel.
